paper_metadata.title: SAPO: Improving the Scalability and Accuracy of Quantum Linear Solver for Portfolio Optimization

experiments.description: SAPO end-to-end HHL-based portfolio optimization evaluated for scalability and accuracy on real market datasets, using constraint scaling and min-max eigenvalue prediction.

algorithm.variant: SAPO (scaled HHL with min-max eigenvalue predictor)

problem_formulation.objective_function: min_w w^T Sigma w subject to s1 w^T R = s1 E and s2 w^T 1 = s2 (equivalent Black's model formulation)
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Equality constraints are scaled by two factors (s1, s2) to form an equivalent Lagrange linear system; HHL solves the resulting linear system.

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization instances derived from real stock-market data; scalability tested from 2 to 6 assets, and accuracy tested under fixed qubit counts and fixed asset counts.

dataset_specification.description: Historical stock prices from Nasdaq/NYSE/AMEX; for training the eigenvalue predictor, 3100 Nasdaq stocks over 251 days are used, with random selection of 3 stocks to construct portfolio instances. Returns are computed from adjacent-day increments; expected return vector and covariance matrix are estimated from historical data; Lagrange matrices are padded to power-of-two size with zeros and identity blocks.

data_preprocessing_details: Compute adjacent-day increments to form return table
Estimate expected return vector and covariance matrix using Eq. (2)
Construct Lagrange matrix from Black's model
Pad Lagrange matrix to power-of-two size with zeros and identity matrix
Standardize Lagrange matrix by l / |lambda|max with l = 0.5
evaluation_methodology: Complexity comparison across asset counts 2-6 and epsilon values 1/16, 1/8, 1/4
Accuracy comparison under fixed 5-qubit QPE across different asset counts
Accuracy comparison under fixed 5-asset problems across different QPE qubit counts
Ablation study for scaling factor and eigenvalue predictor
Eigenvalue predictor error analysis over 1500 cases

implementation_details.classical_solver: SciPy Nelder-Mead for scaling-factor search; scikit-learn SVR for eigenvalue prediction; NumPy for exact eigenvalues
classical_preprocessing: Construct return tables from historical prices
Estimate expected returns and covariance matrices
Train SVR predictor offline on historical data
classical_postprocessing: Measure auxiliary qubit / assume direct access to output state vector
Post-process quantum state to obtain allocation vector

speedup_claims.caveats: Reported as maximum reduction in Table IV; depends on specific instance.

problem_formulation.objective_function: Predict minimum and maximum eigenvalues of the Lagrange matrix from historical financial features

problem_instance.description: Dataset for training and evaluating the eigenvalue predictor, built from randomly selected stock portfolios from Nasdaq, NYSE, and AMEX.

dataset_specification.description: For Nasdaq, 3100 stocks over 251 days are collected; three stocks are randomly selected to form 3-asset portfolio instances. Returns are computed from adjacent-day increments, then expected returns and covariance matrices are used to build the Lagrange matrix. The matrix is padded to power-of-two size before exact min/max eigenvalues are computed with NumPy as labels.

data_preprocessing_details: Estimate expected return vector and covariance matrix
Pad to power-of-two size with zeros and identity matrix
Compute exact min/max eigenvalues with NumPy
evaluation_methodology: Compare SVR against Decision Tree, MLP, and LeNet
Assess relative prediction error over 1500 cases
Analyze accuracy gap induced by predicted eigenvalues

implementation_details.classical_solver: NumPy for exact eigenvalues; scikit-learn for SVR; SciPy for optimization
classical_preprocessing: Feature construction from Lagrange matrix entries
Offline training on historical market data

speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment evaluates a classical SVR predictor used to parameterize HHL, not a quantum runtime speedup.
